title: Record dates with Bobby Sherwood, Red Nichols and Red Norvo
summary: Lovett recalls recording with Julia Lee and these leaders, and using brushes behind Norvo's vibes.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: I'm sure many people must have thought so with the following he's had over the years, which brings us up to these albums. There are so many of them I don't know where to begin. How did -- you know, what kind of -- you worked for Bobby Sherwood quite a bit on the Coast making records.
How was he as a boss?
Oh, wonderful, wonderful, a wonderful person. He was a wonderful person to work for, I'll tell you that much; just everything smooth with him. He doesn't get excited at all and I think --
Oh man, pretty good -- in the meantime Red Nichols was on the deal.
Oh yeah, well you worked with Red Nichols, yes.
How was Red Nichols to work with?
Oh man, it was fine. He used to like a little taste.
And Julia was right with him, you know.
Was Julia on piano in all these?
How did you get -- how did you work your drums in with the vibes of Red Norvell?
Yeah. When you're [fishing] a man, you don't use a whole lot of sticks.
What did you say, when you're fishing a man?
Featuring a man. You don't use the sticks, you know, especially with vibes, you know. You've got to feel with him.
Was Norvo the leader on those or was -- I know he's on quite a few of them. Was he the leader?
